rounds.text: Vivo Bio Tech Ltd trades at a steep discount to its asset backing, with a price-to-book ratio of 0.38x against a book value of ₹ 42.6 and a share price of ₹ 16.4 [E1], heavily discounted compared to the sector benchmark P/B of 2.92x [E6]. Operating momentum shows clear signs of acceleration with trailing twelve-month compounded sales growth reaching 18% [E16], supported by screen signals indicating strong year-on-year sales and profit growth [E55, E57, E58] alongside a supportive healthcare sector tailwind score of +0.78 [E60]. Efficiency of operations is evidenced by robust operating cash flow of Rs 34.93 Cr in March 2026 [E31], paired with a remarkably low EV/EBITDA of 4.75x compared to the sector benchmark of 16.24x [E10]. Future revenue potential is further underscored by capital work-in-progress standing at Rs 16.16 Cr as of September 2026, representing a massive 236.0% increase over the prior year and pointing to a significant growth-spend phase currently underway [E36]. Conceded: promoter holding has dropped to 22.51% as of September 2026 from 42.08% in December 2023 [E37], and return metrics trail sector benchmarks significantly, with ROE at -1.83% versus 10.32% [E8].

Vivo Bio Tech Ltd carries substantial fundamental risks that overshadow its low headline price-to-book multiple [E1]. Compounded sales growth has stagnated at a meager 1% over both 3-year and 5-year periods [E14, E15], accompanied by a catastrophic -164% drop in compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months [E17]. Profitability metrics are deeply distressed, featuring negative ROE figures (-1.83% to -2.2%) [E8, E12] and a low 10-year median ROE of just 6% [E22], alongside explicit flags for a low interest coverage ratio [E49]. Balance sheet pressures are mounting as borrowings climbed to Rs 82.63 Cr in September 2026 from Rs 67.38 Cr a year earlier [E35], dragging the current ratio below parity to 0.94x [E34] and generating negative free cash flow of Rs -2.51 Cr [E32]. Insider commitment has also degraded severely, with promoter holdings plummeting nearly 20 percentage points from 42.08% in December 2023 to 22.51% by September 2026 [E37]. Technical momentum confirms this ongoing deterioration, leaving the stock languishing below both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages [E41] with a dismal Sharpe ratio of -2.48 [E44]. conceded: [E16]

While the bear highlights a stagnant 1% multi-year sales growth rate [E14, E15], it overlooks a clear acceleration with trailing twelve-month sales growth surging to 18% [E16], alongside specific positive momentum signals pointing to 31% YoY sales increases [E55] and 26% YoY net profit gains [E57]. The heavy emphasis on negative return metrics [E8, E12] misses the critical contextual insight from the bias check: results are actively improving with a high results score of 98 out of 100, proving that stale sentiment is masking an unfolding turnaround [E61]. Regarding the rising borrowings [E35], the capital expenditure build-up phase is fully accounted for by a massive 236.0% surge in Capital Work in Progress (CWIP) to Rs 16.16 Cr [E36], reflecting aggressive growth spend rather than distress. conceded: [E17, E32, E37, E41, E49] The extreme cheapness of the stock trading at just 0.38x to 0.39x book value [E1, E48] and an EV/EBITDA of 4.75x against a sector benchmark of 16.24x [E10] provides a massive margin of safety that thoroughly compensates for these transitional balance sheet pressures, especially within a healthcare sector enjoying a strong macro tailwind score of +0.78 [E60].

While the bull points to trailing sales acceleration [E16, E55] and profit gains [E57], it glosses over the catastrophic collapse in compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months, which stands at -164% [E17]. The claim of an active turnaround [E61] is entirely undermined by persistent structural decay: return on equity sits at -2.2% [E12], median ROE over the last year is -2% [E25], and operating margins have compressed by 11 percentage points over four years [E26, E28]. Furthermore, the bull’s dismissal of rising borrowings [E35] through Capital Work in Progress [E36] ignores the immediate strain of a low interest coverage ratio [E49] and a negative free cash flow of Rs -2.51 Cr [E32]. Conceded: [E1, E10, E16, E36, E48, E55, E57, E60, E61]. The heavy reliance on low valuation multiples like a 0.38x price-to-book ratio [E1] fails to account for severe insider abandonment, evidenced by promoters slashing their stake by 19.57 percentage points down to 22.51% [E37], alongside ongoing technical deterioration where the stock trades below both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages [E41].
